I'm a foodie...at least that's what I use as the term to describe myself. Why? Because there isn't a better term available. The traditional term is "gourmet," but let's face it...that reeks of snobbism.

So, let me explain why I use the term. Is it because I eat with wild abandon and would consume anything in sight that's called food? Of course not. To use a parallel, an art collector will not buy just anything just because it's mounted in a frame, and their walls are not plastered with art so thickly that you cannot see the wall behind the hangings.

I celebrate the variety and creativity of exceptional food. Food, when done well and correctly, is art. I cook with an immersion cooker on a regular basis because I love the results. I have dabbled in molecular gastronomy. I'm currently working on being able to reliably (this is the real trick) turn out a perfect French omelet. BUT...I won't go to McDonald's. I won't eat fast food at all unless it's a situation like being on business travel, having half an hour for lunch, and no other options. I see a meal as either an opportunity to celebrate GOOD food...and support it...or a wasted meal where I simply consume just for fuel. I make a good living, so I can choose, and I choose the former. And while the occasional cassoulet is a bit unhealthy and I will eat it from time to time, I do not let food become my enemy. I watch what I eat on the whole, and keep my body and my blood cholesterol as they should be. And really, it's not that hard, especially once you have developed a range of options to choose from.

I have seen places in the world where food is literally life...where you can't be sure how many meals you'll have the following week, and where it's not at all hard to imagine a situation where your entire family would starve to death. I value food, and consider things like Starbuck's Unicorn whatever-the-fuck-that-was as an abomination, an insult. Just as a real art curator would gladly join a mob that took turns holding down Leroy Neiman so that they could piss on his eyeballs, I hate the people who make this garbage, and particularly hate the people who buy it. Their behavior is an affront to the art of good food, and a brazen insult to those elsewhere on this planet who are starving. Not, "muh blood sugar" starving with a BMI of 35, but truly starving.
